population.span: Investigator-initiated, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial among 360 consecutive candidates for cardiac surgery enrolled in 11 Italian centers between March 2012 and March 2014.

endpoint.span: main secondary study end points were postoperative AF and pericardial or pleural effusion

estimate.span: postoperative AF (colchicine, 61 patients [33.9%]; placebo, 75 patients [41.7%]; absolute difference, 7.8%; 95% CI, -2.2% to 17.6%)

ci.span: postoperative AF (colchicine, 61 patients [33.9%]; placebo, 75 patients [41.7%]; absolute difference, 7.8%; 95% CI, -2.2% to 17.6%)

treatment_strategy.span: Patients were randomized to receive placebo (n=180) or colchicine (0.5 mg twice daily in patients ≥70 kg or 0.5 mg once daily in patients <70 kg; n=180) starting between 48 and 72 hours before surgery and continued for 1 month after surgery.

follow_up.span: Post-pericardiotomy syndrome, post-operative effusions, post-operative atrial fibrillation incidence | Incidence of the outcomes at 3 months from cardiac surgery | TIME FRAME: 3 months

absent_reason.analysis_set: No source names the analysis set (ITT / all randomised) for the AF result. The abstract only contrasts it with a 'prespecified on-treatment analysis'; percentages (61/180=33.9%, 75/180=41.7%) are consistent with all 180 randomised per arm, but that is inference, not a stated span.

bound_values.note: counts printed as '61 patients [33.9%]' and '75 patients [41.7%]'; per-arm denominators are not printed in the estimate span (180 per arm is from the randomisation span). Printed CI is for the absolute difference, not for an RR.

entry_population_matches_question.why: Consecutive adult candidates for cardiac surgery (registry: age >18), randomised to perioperative colchicine vs placebo; matches the question population.
entry_population_matches_question.span: Among patients undergoing cardiac surgery, perioperative use of colchicine compared with placebo reduced the incidence of postpericardiotomy syndrome but not of postoperative AF

notes: Only abstract (records.json, europepmc_core.json) and registry held; no full text. Served arm counts (61 vs 75) match the abstract. Served estimand is RR but the source reports only arm counts and an absolute-difference 95% CI (-2.2% to 17.6%); no RR or RR CI is printed, so an RR CI must be computed from counts. Served timepoint label 'in-hospital / index-admission' is not stated in any source; the registry time frame for the outcomes is 3 months (registry span). The alternative on-treatment result (placebo 61/148; colchicine 38/141) was not bound: it is the prespecified on-treatment analysis, not the main comparison. europepmc_core.json text is truncated in the intervention sentence, so records.json was used.
